title: Layer Seven HTTP Reverse Proxy & Load Balancer in Go with Active Health Checks, Least-Connections & Circuit Breaking
problem: Relying on opaque cloud provider load balancers obscures proxy-level concurrency bottlenecks, connection pool starvation, and subtle routing misconfigurations. Naive round-robin reverse proxies route traffic into dead sockets during upstream server crashes, lack connection draining during deployments, and fail to balance heterogeneous backend workloads. This project builds a high-performance Layer Seven application load balancer and reverse proxy from scratch in Go. The system implements multiple load balancing algorithms (round-robin, weighted round-robin, least-connections, and IP-hash), conducts active health checks with circuit breaking, performs graceful upstream draining during rotation, and exports Prometheus metrics.

use_cases.title: Internal Microservice RPC Traffic Balancing
use_cases.first_sentence: Platform engineering teams running private microservice meshes need lightweight, customizable L7 reverse proxies to distribute incoming traffic across backend service instances.
use_cases.second_sentence: The load balancer balances requests using least-connections to ensure long-running computational queries do not overwhelm individual backend pods.

use_cases.title: Zero-Downtime Rolling Upstream Deployment Draining
use_cases.first_sentence: Site reliability engineers require automated connection draining when deploying new application versions to prevent terminating active in-flight HTTP requests.
use_cases.second_sentence: The proxy marks graduating upstreams as draining, completing pending transactions while routing all new client requests to active backend nodes.

use_cases.title: Session-Affinity E-Commerce Checkout Routing
use_cases.first_sentence: E-commerce platforms maintaining in-memory shopping session state need deterministic client routing based on client IP addresses.
use_cases.second_sentence: The proxy implements consistent IP-hashing, mapping identical client IP addresses to dedicated backend instances while gracefully remapping upon backend changes.

hard_parts: Managing high-concurrency Go connection pools with mutex-free atomic counters for least-connections tracking
Designing active asynchronous health check loops that rapidly detect upstream unresponsiveness without overwhelming backends
Implementing graceful upstream draining that awaits in-flight request completions while rejecting new incoming connections
Handling client HTTP keep-alive connection reuse and TCP socket timeouts cleanly under high throughput
screener_signals: Clean idiomatic Go codebase using standard library net/http/httputil primitives, sync/atomic counters, and structured logging
Comprehensive k6 or vegeta load benchmark report validating sub-millisecond proxy latency overhead under 5,000 requests per second
Anti-fake verification script killing a backend upstream during active traffic load and verifying zero dropped requests and immediate route diversion

components.name: Reverse Proxy Engine & Connection Pool Manager
components.purpose: Terminates incoming client connections, manages persistent upstream connection pools, and forwards requests

components.name: Pluggable Algorithm Strategy Selector
components.purpose: Implements round-robin, weighted round-robin, least-connections, and IP-hash routing interfaces

components.name: Active Health Check & Circuit Breaker Engine
components.purpose: Polls backend /health endpoints periodically, detects failures, and trips circuits to isolate dead nodes

components.name: Graceful Upstream Drain Controller
components.purpose: Tracks active in-flight requests per upstream and coordinates zero-downtime draining before server removal

components.name: Prometheus Metrics Exporter & Telemetry Server
components.purpose: Exposes HTTP endpoints serving metrics on active connections, request counts, and upstream response times

architecture.data_flow: Client HTTP requests connect to the Go proxy server; the algorithm selector determines the target upstream server based on the configured strategy (e.g., least-connections); the proxy forwards the request over pooled TCP sockets; in parallel, background health checker goroutines poll each upstream's health endpoint every 2 seconds; if an upstream fails 3 consecutive probes, the circuit breaker removes it from the active pool; when an administrator signals a backend drain, the proxy ceases routing new traffic to that backend while waiting for in-flight requests to finish before closing connections; telemetry metrics update atomically and expose to Prometheus.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: sync/atomic integer counters tracking active connections per upstream; HTTP connection read and write timeouts preventing slowloris socket exhaustion.

targets.method: Wall-clock delta comparing direct upstream latency against proxy-forwarded latency under 5,000 requests per second load
targets.input: 5,000 requests per second sustained HTTP GET workload generated by k6 load tester across 4 upstream servers
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Go 1.21+ release binary, Docker local bridge network
targets.minimum_pass: p95 proxy latency overhead is < 2.0 milliseconds under 5,000 req/sec
targets.target: p95 proxy latency overhead is < 0.85 milliseconds under 5,000 req/sec
targets.report: Proxy benchmark report and k6 latency distribution output

targets.method: Duration from upstream server crash injection to complete removal from active routing table
targets.input: 20 simulated upstream process termination chaos scenarios during active traffic streaming
targets.environment: 4 backend mock HTTP servers running in local Docker containers or background processes
targets.minimum_pass: Average removal duration is < 3.0 seconds with 0 failed requests routed to dead node after removal
targets.target: Average removal duration is < 1.2 seconds with 0 failed requests routed to dead node after removal
targets.report: Active health check timing log and failover verification summary

targets.method: Variance ratio of active concurrent connections across heterogeneous backend nodes with variable processing delays
targets.input: 1,000 simulated requests with variable processing durations (10ms to 200ms) distributed across 4 backends
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Go test suite
targets.minimum_pass: Traffic distribution balance ratio variance is < 15.0% across backends
targets.target: Traffic distribution balance ratio variance is < 6.0% across backends
targets.report: Routing algorithm distribution test log and balance ratio report

riskiest_component.name: Socket File Descriptor Exhaustion Under High Concurrency Load
riskiest_component.mitigation: Configure http.Transport with high MaxIdleConnsPerHost (e.g., 200) and strict IdleConnTimeout.
riskiest_component.fallback: Enable aggressive TCP keep-alive probe intervals and limit maximum concurrent client connections.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a Layer 7 HTTP reverse proxy and load balancer in Go with active health checking, multiple routing algorithms, and Prometheus metrics.
worksheet.q2: Target users: systems software engineers, platform infrastructure architects, and site reliability engineers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: microservice RPC traffic balancing, zero-downtime rolling upstream draining, and session-affinity checkout routing.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: atomic connection counter synchronization, asynchronous health checking without backend flooding, graceful connection draining, and TCP socket lifecycle management.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: Go reverse proxy scaffolding, 4 backend HTTP mock servers, and k6 traffic test suites. Mock HTTP traffic only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: local background processes without Docker.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: socket file descriptor exhaustion under load. Fallback: configure MaxIdleConnsPerHost=200 and strict idle timeouts.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: static round-robin returns. Anti-fake check 5 kills backend during live traffic, asserts 0 failed requests and immediate diversion.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; local loopback mock servers and synthetic traffic only, zero production network interference.
